title: boot on linux: a bad fstab entry drops the system to emergency mode
scenario: On linux, a boot failure: a bad fstab entry drops the system to emergency mode. Symptom: 'emergency mode / dependency failed for /mnt'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'fstab_boot_fail' for boot on linux
expected_reasoning: A failed mount at boot halts into emergency mode; the fstab entry is the suspect, not the kernel.
Boot to a recovery shell, identify the offending entry, make it nofail or fix the device/UUID.
Verify a clean boot; never leave a required mount that can hang boot indefinitely.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'a bad fstab entry drops the system to emergency mode' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('fstab_boot_fail') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Empty /etc/fstab to boot, losing all mount definitions.
Use a device name that changes across boots instead of a UUID.
hints: `nofail` lets boot proceed when a non-critical mount is absent.
alternative_solution: Use a systemd .mount unit with the right dependencies for a complex mount.
edge_cases: The device is fine but the UUID changed after a reformat.
goal: Avvio di sistema: a bad fstab entry drops the system to emergency mode. Ripristina un boot pulito senza reinstallare.
